clue.text: His job involves looking after the kids

definitions.text: His job involves looking after the kids

parts.words: His job involves looking after the kids
parts.note: kids are young goats, not children, so the minder is a herdsman of those animals

explanation.surface: A nanny or childminder describing his working day caring for children.
explanation.definitionFit: A kid is a young goat, so the man who tends a flock of them is the herdsman of goats.

clue.text: Ape a historian

definitions.meaning: a long-armed lesser ape of south-east Asia
Edward ..., author of The Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire

explanation.surface: Telling someone to imitate a historian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ape' looks like a verb meaning copy, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a small tree-dwelling primate and the eighteenth-century English historian Edward Gibbon.

clue.text: Searching investigations, by all accounts

parts.note: by all accounts usually means reportedly, but here it means inspections of every financial account

explanation.surface: Reportedly, thorough inquiries have been carried out.
explanation.definitionFit: These are official examinations of financial records, investigations carried out through the books.

clue.text: Assistance to get to grips with an American's greeting

parts.note: to give a hand is to help
to clasp is to grip firmly

explanation.surface: Help in learning how an American says hello.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans use this term for what Britons call a handshake, the gesture of welcome.

clue.text: Presumably he can be relied upon for dexterity

definitions.text: Presumably he can be relied upon for dexterity

parts.words: Presumably he can be relied upon for dexterity
parts.note: dexterity comes from Latin dexter, right-hand, so the trusted aide is the one on that side

explanation.surface: Describes a reliably skilful worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A chief assistant or trusted deputy; dexterity literally means right-handedness.

clue.text: Row caused by an underwired bra?

definitions.text: Row caused by an underwired bra?

parts.words: Row caused by an underwired bra?
parts.note: a quarrel is a ..., and an underwired bra literally pushes the ...

explanation.surface: A domestic argument blamed on uncomfortable lingerie.
explanation.definitionFit: A bust-up is a noisy quarrel; read literally, it is what supportive underwear does to the chest.

clue.text: Harmony in marriage

definitions.meaning: a wedding joins two people in a formal bond

explanation.surface: Praising a happy, harmonious marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both agreement and accord, and the joining of two people in wedlock.

clue.text: Mythical king who never quite got what he wanted

definitions.text: Mythical king who never quite got what he wanted

parts.words: Mythical king who never quite got what he wanted
parts.note: the Greek king punished in Hades with water and fruit always just out of reach

explanation.surface: A legendary ruler perpetually frustrated.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek king condemned to stand in water that receded and beneath fruit that withdrew whenever he reached; the source of tantalise.

clue.text: Friend with new ideas for making a defence work

parts.note: a pal is a friend

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are made over into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A friend brings fresh ideas for a successful defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges IDEAS into ISADE. 'defence work' reads like a team's defending, but means a fortification.
explanation.definitionFit: A palisade is a fence of stakes built as a fortification.

clue.text: Banter may become hurtful in time

parts.note: something hurtful is bad
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Friendly teasing can turn wounding as time goes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in time' reads as 'eventually', but it splits into the word in, kept as written, and a word for an era.
explanation.definitionFit: Badinage is playful, witty conversation, a close synonym of banter.

clue.text: Remarkable way to communicate

definitions.meaning: as an adjective, ... means striking or notable, as in a ... achievement
a sign or gesture conveying a message

explanation.surface: Praising an extraordinary method of getting a message across.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective sense means notable or outstanding; the noun sense is a gesture or sign that conveys information.

clue.text: Military wit?

definitions.meaning: the military branch gathering information about the enemy

explanation.surface: Asks whether soldiers have a sense of humour.
explanation.definitionFit: The word completes the phrase for armed-forces espionage and also means cleverness or brains.

clue.text: Looker for work has a twitch

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: Someone hunting for a job who suffers from a nervous twitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looker' suggests an attractive person, but here it means something you look with.
explanation.definitionFit: An optic is an eye or lens, the organ or instrument used for looking.

clue.text: Wants one's restored tools

indicators.note: the letters are put back together in a new order, as if repaired

explanation.surface: Someone wants their mended tools returned.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenon saws are fine-toothed woodworking saws used for cutting joints, so they are carpentry implements.

clue.text: It has many stamps on it

definitions.text: It has many stamps on it

parts.words: It has many stamps on it
parts.note: stamps here are soldiers' boots striking the ground in drill, not postage

explanation.surface: Seems to describe an envelope or a stamp album.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill square is where soldiers march and stamp their feet repeatedly.

clue.text: Sort of ruler and a clergyman overseeing several parishes

indicators.note: sort here is a verb, the letters being sorted into a new order

explanation.surface: A kind of measuring stick and a senior churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Church of England this is a priest supervising a deanery, a group of neighbouring parishes.

clue.text: Taught to be literate

explanation.surface: Being schooled in order to read and write.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the past participle of teach's synonym educate, and also an adjective meaning cultured and learned.

clue.text: Length of time around it varied

indicators.note: varied means the letters have been changed into another order

explanation.surface: The time something took fluctuated around a mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: how long something lasts is its span of time.

clue.text: Speed merchants?

parts.note: speed is slang for amphetamine, so those trading it are dealers in narcotics

explanation.surface: Seems to describe fast runners or racing drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Speed is a street name for amphetamine, and merchants are sellers, so these are narcotics dealers.

clue.text: Bluff king and his little successor brought to a stop

parts.note: Bluff King Hal is the traditional nickname of Henry VIII
Henry VIII was succeeded by his son Edward VI, and Ted is a pet form of Edward

explanation.surface: A hearty monarch and his young heir are halted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bluff King Hal' is the popular name for Henry VIII; his son Edward VI, a boy king, followed him.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to be stopped is to be made to stand still.

clue.text: Greek ferry operator taking late arrivals

definitions.text: Greek ferry operator taking late arrivals

parts.words: Greek ferry operator taking late arrivals
parts.note: late here means dead, so the passengers are souls of the departed crossing the Styx

explanation.surface: A ferry company in Greece letting latecomers aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth he is the boatman who carries the souls of the dead across the river Styx.

clue.text: Prisoners closely linked at work

parts.note: convicts shackled together while labouring outdoors

explanation.surface: Inmates who collaborate closely on the job.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain gang is a group of convicts fettered together while doing hard labour.

clue.text: Strange thing, but it's time for bed

indicators.note: strange indicates the letters are made peculiar, rearranged

explanation.surface: Something odd is happening, but it's bedtime.
explanation.definitionFit: The hours of darkness are when people sleep.

clue.text: The French male remains in control

parts.note: le is the masculine form of the definite article in French
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's ashes kept in someone's charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog's lead is the means of restraint, and to hold someone on a lead is to keep them in check.

clue.text: Objects to nights being disturbed

indicators.note: the letters of the word are disturbed, jumbled out of order

explanation.surface: Someone protests at having their sleep interrupted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Objects' looks like a verb meaning protests, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: objects are items or articles.

clue.text: An odd escort for an older person

indicators.note: odd suggests the letters of the word are in a strange order

explanation.surface: A peculiar chaperone for an elderly companion.
explanation.definitionFit: A forebear is someone from an earlier generation, so very much an elder.

clue.text: Give fruit on entering

indicators.note: the word on enters, going inside the fruit word

parts.note: a date is the fruit of the date palm

explanation.surface: Handing over fruit at the door.
explanation.definitionFit: To donate is to give something, typically to charity.

clue.text: Gangly English teacher put under pressure

parts.note: a gangly person is thin, lean
a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: A lanky English schoolmaster being harassed.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to lean on someone is to pressure or intimidate them.
